overview: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, between Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. Its capital and largest city is Minsk. Belarus was part of the Soviet Union until it became independent in 1991. Belarusian and Russian are both official languages.

geography.text: Belarus is mostly flat and low, with no mountains. Forests cover around 40 percent of the land, and the south contains part of the Polesia marshes, one of the largest wetlands in Europe. The country has thousands of lakes, the biggest being Lake Narach, and its main rivers include the Dnieper, the Neman and the Western Dvina.

history.text: The lands of Belarus were part of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and later the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, before being absorbed into the Russian Empire in the late 1700s. Belarus suffered terribly in the Second World War, losing around a quarter of its population. It became independent when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.

events.title: Union of Lublin
events.text: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania, including Belarusian lands, joins with Poland in one commonwealth.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: The last partition of Poland–Lithuania puts all of Belarus inside the Russian Empire.

events.title: End of German occupation
events.text: Belarus is freed from three years of devastating German occupation.

events.title: Chernobyl disaster
events.text: Much of the radioactive fallout from the accident in Ukraine lands on Belarus.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Belarus becomes independent as the Soviet Union breaks up.

government.text: Belarus is officially a presidential republic, but power is concentrated in the hands of the President. Alexander Lukashenko has held the office since 1994. International observers have not judged its elections free and fair, and mass protests after the 2020 election were met with arrests. Belarus is a close ally of Russia.

economy.text: Belarus kept much of its economy under state control after the Soviet Union broke up. It makes tractors, trucks, fertiliser and refined oil products, and it relies heavily on cheap Russian oil and gas and on trade with Russia. Western sanctions have tightened since 2020.

culture.text: Belarusian and Russian are both official languages, and Russian is the one most people use day to day. The country has many medieval castles and wooden churches. Marc Chagall, the painter known for his dreamlike floating figures, grew up in Vitebsk.

items.title: Mir and Nesvizh castles
items.text: Two castles of the old Grand Duchy of Lithuania, both listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Białowieża Forest
items.text: One of Europe's last ancient forests, shared with Poland and home to European bison.

items.title: Marc Chagall
items.text: The artist was born near Vitebsk in 1887.

sport.text: Ice hockey is the most popular sport in Belarus. The country has done well in biathlon, gymnastics and wrestling, and the tennis player Aryna Sabalenka became world number one in 2023.

items.text: Belarus reached the Olympic ice hockey semi-final after a famous win over Sweden.

items.title: Biathlon
items.text: Darya Domracheva won three gold medals at the 2014 Winter Olympics.
